newsitem.title: USA: U.S. will weigh Boskin committee views on CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. will weigh Boskin committee views on CPI.

text.p: A top U.S. official said on Tuesday the administration would study the Boskin commission's recommendations on whether it should change how it calculates the consumer price index (CPI), but would also seek the views of other economists.

Office and Management and Budget Director Franklin Raines said the administration wants to know if there is a consensus among experts, including the commission chaired by Stanford economist Michael Boskin, that changes be made in the CPI.
"We will read it (the Boskin report) with interest. We'll also want to know what other economists who aren't on the commission think about the same issues," Raines told a small group of reporters.
"If the expert opinion is that there are additional changes that should be made, then we'll be supportive of changes that will make the index more accurate," he added.

The Senate Finance Committee has said it will release the bipartisan Boskin commission's final report on December 4. A preliminary report, released in September, said that the CPI overstates inflation by between 0.7 and 2.0 percent.
